JUDGMENT
The PSI of Ashoknagar Police Station submitted charge sheet against the accused person for the offences punishable under sections 408 and 420 of IPC.

. The brief facts of the prosecution case is as follows:-
The case of the prosecution is that the complainant is running a travel business in the name and style of M/s Sri Sri Business Links at No.46, Shanthinagar Swasti Road,
Bengaluru, wherein the complainant books Train Tickets, Air Tickets, Bus Tickets and Mobile Recharging and also having received the money through Via.Com.
It is alleged that the accused was working in this company and she is looking all the business transaction.

In between from 01.09.2015 to 20.07.2018 she is booked tickets through Via.com website to the customers and collected money through cash and not credited the same to the company account and thereafter she was shown the false account details to the complainant and she has transferred money through Via.com to her account and others bank account and thereby she had misappropriated an amount of Rs.7,11,117/- and misused for her personal use and thereby the accused persons have committed the criminal breach of trust and cheated the complainant and committed the above offences.

After completion of the investigation the PSI of Ashoknagar Police Station has filed the charge sheet against the C.C.No.13631/2019 accused person for the offences punishable under sections 408 and 420 of IPC.
3.
Thereafter, the complainant has lodged the complaint in Ashoknagar Police station.
In turn they have registered the case under Crime No.0345/2018.
Thereafter, police visited the spot, drew the mahazar, secured in the presence of the accused person subsequently the accused person enlarged on bail.

Thereafter, on completion of the investigation, I.O. has submitted the charge sheet against Hanamantha Reddy vs Harshitha S on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34143708/
2 the accused person for the above said offences.
After filing the charge sheet, Court has taken cognizance of the offences against the accused person and issued summons to her.
4. The accused person has appeared before the court through her counsel.
Copy of the prosecution papers were furnished under Section 207 of Code of Criminal procedure.
Thereafter, heard both side.
The charges framed against the accused person for the offences punishable under sections 406 and 420 of IPC.

Read over and explained to the accused person and was pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
C.C.No.13631/2019 5.
To substantiate the case of the prosecution, the prosecution have examined the one witness as PW-1 and got marked three documents as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-3.
The accused person did not choose to lead defense evidence.
The statement of the accused person under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., is dispensed with.

6. Heard the arguments from both side and perused the deposition and documents.
7.
After hearing the parties and on perusal of records, the following points arose for my consideration.

1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the complainant is running a travel business in the name and style of M/s Sri Sri Business Links at No.46, Shanthinagar Swasti Road, Bengaluru, wherein the complainant books Train Tickets, Air Tickets, Bus Tickets and Mobile Recharging and also having received the money through Via.Com.
It is alleged that the accused was working in this company C.C.No.13631/2019 and she is looking all the business transaction.

In between from 01.09.2015 to 20.07.2018 she is booked tickets through Via.com website to the customers and collected money through cash and not credited the same to the company account and thereafter she was shown the false account details to the complainant and she has transferred money through Via.com to her account and others bank account and thereby she had misappropriated an amount of Rs.7,11,117/- and committed the criminal breach of trust for the offence punishable under section 406 of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the above said date, place and time that the accused person for the purpose of cheating in between from 01.09.2015 to 20.07.2018 she is booked tickets through Via.com website to the C.C.No.13631/2019 customers and collected money through cash and not credited the same to the company account and thereafter she was shown the false account details to the complainant and she has transferred money through Via.com to her account and others bank account and thereby she had cheated the complainant company an amount of Rs.7,11,117/- and committed the offence punishable under section 420 of IPC?
3. What order?
8. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on records.

My findings to the above points are as follows:
 POINT No.1 : In the NEGATIVE.
 POINT No.2 : In the NEGATIVE.

POINT No.3 : As per final order, for the  following:-

Point Nos.1 and 2: These above points are inter- linked with each others and required similar type of appreciation of evidence, Hence, they are taken together for common discussion.

11. In support of its case, the prosecution has examined one witness, the PW-1 is the complainant and got marked three documents i.e., Ex.P-1 is the Complaint, Ex.P-2 is the Mahazar and Ex.P-3 is the restatement of PW-1.

12. The case of the prosecution is that the complainant is running a travel business in the name and style of M/s Sri Sri Business Links at No.46, Shanthinagar Swasti Road, Bengaluru, wherein the complainant books Train Tickets, Air Tickets, Bus Tickets and Mobile Recharging and also having received the money through Via.Com.
It is alleged that the accused was working in this company and she is looking all the business transaction.

In between from 01.09.2015 to 20.07.2018 she is booked tickets through Via.com website to the customers and collected money through cash and not credited the same to the company account and thereafter she C.C.No.13631/2019 was shown the false account details to the complainant and she has transferred money through Via.com to her account and others bank account and thereby she had misappropriated an amount of Rs.7,11,117/-
and misused for her personal use and thereby the accused persons have committed the criminal breach of trust and cheated the complainant and committed the above offences.
After completion of the investigation the PSI of Ashoknagar Police Station has filed the charge sheet against the accused person for the offences punishable under sections 408 and 420 of IPC.
13. In the instant case the PW-1 has turned hostile to the prosecution case and not supported to the prosecution case.
During the course of cross examination by the learned Sr. APP nothing has been elicited from her mouth.
14. In this case, the prosecution has failed to elicit anything favorable to it to prove the allegations against the accused person under sections 406 and 420 of IPC.
When these being the facts, I am of the opinion that in total the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused C.C.No.13631/2019 person beyond all reasonable doubt.
In view of the same, this court hold Point Nos.1 and 2 in the Negative.
15. Point No.3: For the reasons stated and finding given to point Nos.1 and 2, the following is made.

4 ORDER
The accused person is not found guilty for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC.
Acting under section 248(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure the accused person is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond executed by her stand canceled.
